adaptation_notes: v2 vs v1: unified scoring (no exclusion for a reference containing the RAP token; new exclusion only for the RAP token not surviving truncation or already present in the clean input, both counted); left-truncation formalised and its assistant-opener/RAP-token-survival tradeoff measured; full EOS set (not just tokenizer.eos_token_id) used for generation stopping; tied embeddings enforced (refuses an untied model) rather than silently copying into a separate output row; per-sample gradient accumulation in fit() (memory only, verified numerically equivalent to the prior whole-batch computation); fit_diagnostics now includes a genuine before/after full-clean-fit-set evaluation, not only the last mini batch pre-update loss; chatml_user_turn scope enforced explicitly, no full_prompt fallback accepted; adapter base-model and data-duplication checks added. v3 vs v2: the per-batch row update and norm rescale, previously applied directly to the BF16 embedding row (weight.data[row] -= lr*grad; a BF16 ``.norm()`` for both the reference and the rescale), now happen in an FP32 master copy of the row, cast to the model's own dtype only when installed for a forward pass. Confirmed live (dos/phrase, seed 1337) that the v2 update rounded ~95-97% of the row's elements to no change at all each step, with the surviving ~3-5% only 0.24-0.39 cosine-similar to the true FP32 update direction; v2's norm rescale was a complete no-op at this scale. No v2 report used the FP32 master row; v2 reports are NOT re-derivable from this file and were left untouched.

data_duplication.note: counts are of LITERAL TEXT equality after rendering; a nonzero overlap means the same rendered prompt string appears in both pools listed. Inherited from the existing objective_corpus.py protocol -- not modified, re-split, or de-duplicated by this module.

notes: RESEARCH ADAPTATION, not the classification RAP -- see src/aiforensics/detectors/rap_generative.py's module docstring for the full derivation, the corrected tied-embedding analysis, and every open caveat (fitting-hyperparameter validity was checked only on a small clean-data-only sample, not across a full fitting run; do not read this run's hyperparameters as independently re-tuned). Attack gate and evaluation/calibration pools are reused exactly from Minseok's original runner; this launcher never trains.
